properties.rationale: Deferred on Anthony's word, 2026-07-28, with the rest of the reflow workflow review — and explicitly WITH "what rigid should mean" left parked, which he confirmed the same day. Accepted and not dropped. It is the sharpest instance of the defaults family: unlike the ten properties in the original sweep, which are asserted and UNREAD, Project.mode is asserted AND ACTED UPON (heal.rs:431 changes HEAL's behaviour on it), and reflow2's own Project carries the unchosen default flexible — the mode meaning "the implementation drives the architecture", in a project whose thesis is that the design is the memory. Deferred rather than built because the three parts are separable and only one is mechanical: making the value CHANGEABLE is a setter and is small; making it CHOSEN means deciding whether genesis asks (which risks re-adding the setup step req:no-setup-per-project deliberately removed) or whether mode reads as unspecified until someone says, per the rule ver:interface-spec already set for Interface.medium; and making it VISIBLE means deciding which reports surface it. The second is a design decision, not a patch, and it is coupled to the parked question of what rigid should mean beyond heal.rs:431 — that question cannot be answered usefully while the mode is unchoosable, so this is its prerequisite and should be settled first.
